claim: fullWindowCount is only assigned inside the @-modifier reuse guard, so for @-modified matrix selectors reused across steps it stays 0 and IncrementSamplesAtStep adds nothing, silently under-counting totalQueryableSamples / prometheus_engine_query_samples_total. Measured: predict_linear(x[60s] @ 30, 3600) over a 4-step range query reports TotalSamples 4 at head vs 16 at base.
raw: 🟠 High: `totalQueryableSamples` / `prometheus_engine_query_samples_total` silently changes value for `@`-modified matrix selectors

claim: evalSubquery calls MergeSamplesReadFromSubquery to fold subquery storage reads into the parent, but the caller then materializes the subquery result and walks it with the per-step loop calling IncrementSamplesReadAtStep, charging the same samples to SamplesRead twice. Measured: max_over_time(m3[60s:5s]) gives TotalSamples 36, SamplesRead 72, so samplesRead exceeds totalQueryableSamples.
raw: 🟠 High: subquery samples are counted twice in `SamplesRead`, so `samplesRead` exceeds `totalQueryableSamples`

claim: stats.NewChildWithStepTracking allocates two []int64 sized by the subquery step count before evaluation, so query.max-samples cannot bound it; max_over_time(foo[10m:1ms]) allocates 9.7 MB even when the query aborts after 10 samples (base: 96 KB), scaling linearly with subquery resolution.
raw: 🟠 High: subquery step-tracking arrays are allocated proportional to subquery step count, before and regardless of `query.max-samples`

claim: countSamplesAfter walks the entire sorted floats/histograms slice per series per step in the hottest PromQL loop, an O(window) scan where binary search suffices, and the cost is paid unconditionally even when stats are disabled. BenchmarkRangeQuery rate(a_one[1d]) steps=1000 regresses ~5.80 ms to ~9.09 ms (+57%).
raw: 🟠 High: `countSamplesAfter` adds an O(window) linear scan per step to the hottest PromQL loop, paid even when stats are disabled

claim: The documented invariant that samplesRead equals totalQueryableSamples for non-range-vector-function queries is false for step-invariant (@) expressions: engine.go:2472 adds the step-invariant subtree's SamplesRead once at step 0 while TotalSamples is distributed across every step. Measured: m3 @ 30 over a range query gives TotalSamples 12, SamplesRead 3. All three sites stating the invariant (both docs and the SamplesRead field comment) are wrong.
raw: 🟡 Medium: the documented invariant "for other query types, `samplesRead` equals `totalQueryableSamples`" is false for step-invariant (`@`) expressions
